base.analysis_integration: The PCA-based analysis of the grid STS datacube on TaS2 identifies three actionable physics questions that the current data cannot resolve because PCA loadings are variance eigenvectors, not absolute LDOS: (1) whether the dominant periodic superlattice (likely a sqrt13 x sqrt13 CDW) coexists with a genuine zero-bias gap (Mott vs. CDW gap) — this requires the actual mean/averaged dI/dV spectrum with high energy resolution near E_F; (2) whether the diagonal linear feature picked out by Components 3 and 4 represents genuine boundary-localized electronic structure versus a topographic step-edge/registration/tip artifact — this requires comparing real mean spectra on either side of, and across, the boundary, ideally decoupled from topographic crosstalk; and (3) whether Component 5's localized feature is a true minority/defect state. The novelty-relevant open debates (CDW+Mott coexistence, domain-wall conducting channels) map directly onto these gaps. I therefore prioritize measurements that recover ground-truth spectra (not just variance patterns), disentangle instrumental artifacts flagged in the analysis (Component 2 streaking, bipolar derivative shapes from registration mismatch), and add correlative/temperature context. The energy window and bias resolution are tuned to the specific features observed (-0.3 V peak, +0.3-0.4 V shoulder, -0.55 V and +0.4-0.7 V features in Component 5, and the near-zero-bias region critical for gap determination).

measurement_recommendations.description: Acquire high-energy-resolution grid or line dI/dV spectra with a tightened bias window and denser sampling around the Fermi level, using a lower lock-in modulation amplitude (e.g., 1-2 mV) and lower temperature to sharpen features. Report the true spatially-averaged mean dI/dV spectrum (not PCA loadings) to test for a zero-bias suppression/gap.
measurement_recommendations.target_regions: Bias window -0.6 to +0.6 V with ~2-5 mV steps; emphasize -0.1 to +0.1 V for gap edges and the observed -0.3 V peak and +0.3 to +0.4 V shoulder.
measurement_recommendations.scientific_justification: The dominant Component 1 loading shows reduced weight near zero bias but a PCA eigenvector cannot distinguish a Mott gap, CDW gap, or simple LDOS minimum. Only the actual mean spectrum with fine energy resolution near E_F can establish whether a gap exists and estimate its magnitude, directly addressing the CDW+Mott coexistence debate.
measurement_recommendations.expected_outcomes: A ground-truth mean dI/dV curve revealing presence/absence and width of a Fermi-level gap, sharpened CDW-derived peak positions, and quantitative gap-edge energies to discriminate Mott vs. CDW-gap scenarios.

target.setting: Bias sweep -0.6 V to +0.6 V, 2 mV steps (~600 points), lock-in modulation 1-2 mV RMS
target.expected_signature: Depressed dI/dV within roughly +/-100 meV of zero bias (gap) flanked by the -0.3 V CDW peak and +0.3-0.4 V shoulder in the true mean spectrum

measurement_recommendations.description: Perform a high-spatial-resolution grid STS scan on a narrow region straddling the diagonal linear feature, acquiring simultaneous topography (constant-current) and dI/dV so mean spectra can be compared point-by-point across the boundary, decoupling topographic crosstalk from electronic changes.
measurement_recommendations.target_regions: A 3x5 nm region centered on the diagonal linear feature highlighted by Components 3 and 4, with dense line profiles crossing the boundary perpendicularly.
measurement_recommendations.scientific_justification: The bipolar/derivative-like PCA components along the diagonal are ambiguous: they could indicate genuine boundary-localized (domain-wall/step-edge) electronic states or arise from step-edge convolution, registration mismatch, or tip effects. Comparing actual mean spectra on either side, with co-registered topography, is the definitive test.
measurement_recommendations.expected_outcomes: Determination of whether spectra shift rigidly (topographic/registration artifact) or show genuinely modified gap-edge states localized at the boundary; identification of the feature as domain wall vs. step edge vs. CDW domain boundary.

target.setting: 168x168 px over 3x5 nm across the diagonal feature; simultaneous topo + dI/dV, bias -0.6 to +0.6 V
target.expected_signature: Either a rigid energy offset of the mean spectrum across the boundary (artifact) or new/enhanced in-gap or gap-edge states confined within ~1-2 nm of the line (genuine boundary state)

measurement_recommendations.description: Repeat grid STS with orthogonal (rotated 90 degrees) and reversed slow-scan directions and re-image the same area to test whether the diagonal feature and Component 2 streaking are scan-direction/drift artifacts or physically fixed to the lattice.
measurement_recommendations.target_regions: Same 15x15 nm region; identical bias range; alternate fast/slow scan axis orientation and scan direction.
measurement_recommendations.scientific_justification: The analysis explicitly flags horizontal streaking (drift/lock-in noise) in Component 2 and notes that scan-axis gradients can mimic derivative-like components. Scan-direction control experiments are the standard, low-cost way to separate instrumental artifacts from real electronic structure.
measurement_recommendations.expected_outcomes: Confirmation of whether the linear feature and bipolar components are pinned to the sample (physical) or to the scan geometry (artifact), validating or refuting the domain-wall interpretation.

target.setting: Two grid acquisitions with fast-scan axis rotated 90 degrees relative to original, identical bias/resolution
target.expected_signature: A physical boundary remains fixed to the atomic/CDW lattice across orientations; an artifact rotates/translates with the scan axis

measurement_recommendations.description: Acquire correlative atomically-resolved constant-current topography (and, if available, non-contact AFM or Fourier-filtered lattice mapping) over the same area to independently quantify the superlattice geometry and confirm the sqrt13xsqrt13 Star-of-David reconstruction and identify defects underlying Component 5.
measurement_recommendations.target_regions: Full 15x15 nm field plus zoom-in on the localized Component 5 region and along the diagonal boundary.
measurement_recommendations.scientific_justification: The polytype and reconstruction geometry are currently inferred, not established. Direct real-space and reciprocal-space (FFT) determination of superlattice vectors relative to the atomic lattice, plus defect imaging, will confirm the CDW geometry and clarify whether Component 5 arises from a specific defect.
measurement_recommendations.expected_outcomes: Quantitative superlattice periodicity and rotation angle confirming (or refuting) sqrt13xsqrt13 order; identification of the atomic/defect origin of the localized Component 5 feature.

target.setting: Constant-current topography at low bias (e.g., +50 to +100 mV, 100 pA) with atomic resolution; FFT analysis of superlattice vectors
target.expected_signature: FFT peaks at sqrt13xsqrt13 positions rotated ~13.9 degrees from atomic Bragg peaks; discrete defects co-located with Component 5 intensity

measurement_recommendations.description: Conduct temperature-dependent grid STS across the CDW transition range, tracking evolution of the superlattice periodicity, the near-E_F gap, and the diagonal boundary feature to identify transition temperatures and dynamics.
measurement_recommendations.target_regions: Same 15x15 nm field; temperature series spanning nominal CDW/Mott transition temperatures for 1T-TaS2 (e.g., ~180-350 K, plus low-T base); bias -0.6 to +0.6 V.
measurement_recommendations.scientific_justification: Distinguishing CDW-gap from Mott-gap and confirming the sqrt13xsqrt13 origin is greatly aided by observing how the superlattice and gap respond to temperature; domain walls may act as nucleation sites for phase transitions, testable via their thermal behavior.
measurement_recommendations.expected_outcomes: Transition temperatures for CDW order and gap opening/closing; evidence for whether the boundary feature nucleates or pins phase transitions; discrimination between correlation-driven and CDW-driven gap.

target.setting: Grid STS at ~5-6 set temperatures (e.g., base, 180 K, 220 K, 300 K, 350 K), bias -0.6 to +0.6 V
target.expected_signature: Gap closure and superlattice amplitude reduction above the CDW/Mott transition; hysteretic or boundary-nucleated changes near the domain wall

hist.analysis_integration: The PCA analysis produced two central physical hypotheses that are currently under-determined by the data because PCA loadings are variance eigenvectors and cannot be read as absolute LDOS. First, Component 1's ordered superlattice map strongly suggests a CDW superstructure, but the claimed zero-bias suppression (potential Mott/CDW gap) cannot be confirmed without the actual mean dI/dV spectrum. Second, Components 3/4 concentrate along a diagonal linear feature (possible domain wall/step edge), but their derivative-like character is equally consistent with a registration/step-edge/tip artifact — Component 2's horizontal streaking underscores this risk. The novelty questions ('Has anyone observed a CDW superlattice coexisting with a Mott gap?' and 'Has anyone detected shifted gap-edge states along domain walls?') map directly onto these two open issues. Therefore my recommendations prioritize (1) obtaining true mean/point spectra to test the gap hypothesis, (2) spatially resolved point-spectroscopy comparison across the boundary to distinguish genuine electronic reconstruction from artifact, (3) higher-resolution/low-bias energy refinement to characterize any gap edge, (4) temperature-dependent measurement to test the CDW/Mott origin, and (5) correlative bias-dependent topography to establish CDW geometry. These convert exploratory PCA patterns into physically decisive measurements.

measurement_recommendations.description: Acquire high-energy-resolution point dI/dV spectra (dense bias sampling, longer lock-in integration, lower lock-in modulation amplitude ~1-2 mV) at representative sites: on a CDW superlattice maximum, on a superlattice minimum, and away from the boundary. Report absolute mean dI/dV, not PCA loadings.
measurement_recommendations.target_regions: Bias window -0.6 to +0.6 V with fine sampling near zero bias (-0.2 to +0.2 V); spatial sites on Component 1 bright maxima vs minima.
measurement_recommendations.scientific_justification: The central open question is whether the near-zero-bias weight reduction seen in the PCA loading corresponds to a real Fermi-level gap (Mott or CDW-derived). Only the true mean dI/dV spectrum can establish gap presence, magnitude, and symmetry — the PCA loading cannot.
measurement_recommendations.expected_outcomes: Definitive determination of whether a gap exists at E_F, its width and shape (hard vs soft, particle-hole symmetry), enabling discrimination between a Mott gap, CDW gap, or simple LDOS minimum.

target.setting: Bias sweep -0.6 to +0.6 V, ~4-5 mV steps, lock-in modulation 1-2 mV, extended dwell; point spectra at 3+ CDW registry sites
target.expected_signature: A reproducible suppression of dI/dV centered at 0 V with defined gap edges (e.g. peaks near +/-0.15-0.3 V) confirming a genuine gap, versus a shallow non-zero minimum indicating no true gap

measurement_recommendations.description: Acquire a line-cut series of point dI/dV spectra crossing the diagonal linear feature perpendicularly, sampling equal numbers of points on each side and directly on the boundary, with identical setpoint and integration to eliminate scan-direction/registration gradients.
measurement_recommendations.target_regions: A perpendicular transect (~5-8 nm) across the diagonal feature where Components 3 and 4 concentrate; -0.6 to +0.6 V bias.
measurement_recommendations.scientific_justification: Components 3/4's bipolar loadings could reflect a genuine electronic reconstruction along a domain wall OR a topographic step-edge/registration/tip artifact. Comparing true mean spectra on either side of the boundary is the only way to distinguish a real energy shift/gap-edge modification from an instrumental convolution.
measurement_recommendations.expected_outcomes: A spatially resolved map of any rigid energy shift or gap-edge redistribution across the boundary; if spectra shift smoothly with topography it indicates step-edge convolution, whereas an abrupt distinct spectral signature indicates genuine boundary-localized electronic structure.

target.setting: Line spectroscopy, ~40-60 points across boundary, bias -0.6 to +0.6 V, fixed setpoint (e.g. 100 pA at +0.5 V), single scan direction
target.expected_signature: Either an abrupt localized peak/gap-edge state confined to the boundary (genuine reconstruction) or a monotonic shift tracking topography (artifact)

measurement_recommendations.description: Repeat grid STS over the same region at multiple sample temperatures spanning the expected CDW/Mott transition (e.g. cool from ~78 K toward ~4 K, and warm toward ~180-350 K depending on cryostat range) to observe evolution of the superlattice and any gap.
measurement_recommendations.target_regions: Same 15x15 nm region; focus bias -0.4 to +0.4 V for gap tracking; temperatures bracketing known 1T-TaS2 commensurate/nearly-commensurate transitions.
measurement_recommendations.scientific_justification: 1T-TaS2 exhibits temperature-dependent CDW phases (commensurate, nearly-commensurate) and a Mott gap that collapses with temperature. Tracking the superlattice amplitude and gap versus temperature directly tests the CDW/Mott origin hypothesis and the polytype assignment.
measurement_recommendations.expected_outcomes: Identification of transition temperatures, correlation of gap opening with CDW commensuration, and confirmation (or rejection) of the 1T-Mott picture versus alternative polytypes.

target.setting: Grid STS at 3+ temperatures (e.g. 4.5 K, 78 K, 200 K), bias -0.4 to +0.4 V emphasis
target.expected_signature: Progressive filling of the zero-bias gap and weakening/change of superlattice periodicity as temperature increases through the transition

measurement_recommendations.description: Acquire bias-dependent constant-current topography maps at several fixed biases (filled-state and empty-state imaging) over the same region to correlate the CDW superlattice geometry and boundary topography with the STS-derived electronic maps.
measurement_recommendations.target_regions: Same 15x15 nm region; imaging biases e.g. -0.3 V (near the PCA peak), +0.35 V (shoulder), and near zero-bias-edge biases; focus on the diagonal feature.
measurement_recommendations.scientific_justification: Bias-dependent topography reveals whether the superlattice contrast reverses or shifts with energy (fingerprint of CDW electronic modulation and Star-of-David geometry) and whether the diagonal feature is a physical step (height change) versus a purely electronic domain wall — directly testing the artifact-vs-reconstruction ambiguity.
measurement_recommendations.expected_outcomes: Confirmation of CDW superlattice periodicity/geometry (e.g. sqrt13xsqrt13) via bias-dependent contrast, and determination of whether the diagonal line is a topographic step edge (measurable height) or an electronic domain wall.

target.setting: Constant-current topography at fixed biases -0.3 V, +0.35 V, and +/-0.1 V; 15x15 nm; measure apparent height across the diagonal feature
target.expected_signature: Energy-dependent superlattice contrast reversal (CDW signature) and a step in apparent height at the boundary if it is topographic, or no height change if purely electronic

measurement_recommendations.description: Acquire a higher-spatial-resolution grid STS zoom (e.g. 128x128 px over 4x4 nm) centered on Component 5's localized region and an isolated segment of the diagonal boundary, to resolve atomic-scale registry of any defect/minority state relative to the CDW lattice.
measurement_recommendations.target_regions: The small localized region carrying Component 5 weight and an adjacent boundary segment; full -1.0 to +1.0 V bias but emphasize -0.7 to +0.7 V.
measurement_recommendations.scientific_justification: Component 5 suggests a candidate minority phase or defect-localized state with features near -0.55 V and +0.4 to +0.7 V. Higher spatial resolution is needed to determine whether this is pinned to a specific defect, a CDW dislocation, or the boundary, and to relate it to the atomic/superlattice registry.
measurement_recommendations.expected_outcomes: Atomic-scale localization of the Component 5 state, distinguishing a point-defect resonance from a boundary-derived state, and confirming whether it is a reproducible minority phase.

target.setting: Grid STS 128x128 px over 4x4 nm centered on Component 5 hotspot, bias -0.7 to +0.7 V
target.expected_signature: Spatially confined dI/dV resonances near -0.55 V and +0.4 to +0.7 V localized to a defect site or CDW dislocation core

history: Grid STS dI/dV cube, 168x168 px over 15x15 nm, bias -1.0 to +1.0 V (151 pts) — the analyzed cube
